prompt: In many countries, plastic bags are the main source of rubbish, causing pollution in oceans and on land; therefore, they should be banned. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement?
essay:
It is widely believed that synthetic carrier bags cause a major portion of municipal waste and inflict severe ecological damage on both land and water bodies. It is frequently suggested that they must be outlawed. I firmly agree that implementing an outright ban on these items is a necessary measure to protect global ecosystems.

Plastic bags damage marine and land ecosystems because they persist for centuries and injure wildlife through ingestion or entanglement. These bags do not break down easily, so they stay in nature for a very long time and become a serious danger. For example, the documentary film by BBC Earth shows that many marine species, such as sea turtles and seabirds, wash ashore with stomachs full of non-biodegradable plastic fragments. This clearly proves that plastic packets harm animals and pollute both oceans and land.

In addition, banning plastic bags drives widespread behavioural shifts and forces consumers and businesses to adopt sustainable, eco-friendly alternatives like cloth or biodegradable bags. When governments restrict these carriers, people start using reusable options and companies also change their habits. A good real-life example is Singapore’s nationwide ban on single-use plastic bags introduced twenty years ago. This policy successfully transformed the country into one of the cleanest and most environmentally conscious nations in Asia. Such a ban can therefore create a greener lifestyle for everyone.

In conclusion environmental degradation caused by non-biodegradable waste has become one of the most pressing crises of the modern era. Plastic carriers, in particular, are notorious for clogging landfills and polluting natural habitats. I absolutely agree with the idea of prohibiting single-use plastic packages, as they can harm wildlife and banning them leads us to a cleaner future.
